# One: The Island

The lighthouse stands at the far end of a narrow island, about two miles off the coast. For more than a hundred years it has warned ships away from the rocks that hide just under the surface at high tide.

The first keeper arrived in the spring with his wife, two goats, and a crate of books. He wrote in his logbook every single evening, even on nights when nothing happened at all.

> PAUSE: Can you hear me clearly so far?

# Two: The Storm

In the winter of the third year, a storm came in from the north and lasted for nine days. The waves climbed higher than the keeper had ever seen, and spray rattled against the glass at the top of the tower.

On the fourth night the main lamp went dark. He climbed the spiral stairs with a lantern in one hand and a box of spare wicks in the other, counting every step so he would not lose his footing.

He relit the lamp just before midnight. Out in the dark, a fishing boat that had been drifting toward the rocks turned sharply and made its way safely into the harbor.

# Three: The Letters

Years later, the captain of that boat wrote a letter to the keeper. He said that he had given up hope that night, and that the light appearing out of nowhere had felt like a small miracle.

The keeper kept the letter folded inside his logbook. When he retired, he left the logbook on the desk for the next keeper, with a note that said simply: read the page from the fourth night.

> BRANCH: Do you want to hear what happened to the lighthouse?
>> YES
Today the lamp runs on its own, powered by solar panels, and no one lives on the island anymore. Visitors can take a ferry out in the summer and climb the same spiral stairs.
